verdicts.misleading_risk: Medium. A 'Description complete' label next to Community/Verified will be read as a quality mark, and the 4 real apps would all show 'Missing: ...' before their authors can fill fields that do not exist yet (inputs/outputs/status etc. are not in the vendored schemas). Hard-gating NEW submissions on 9 tier-2 items while 0 of the 4 existing apps meet them means no real author could pass the bot; the bot would reject apps the maintainers themselves have not made compliant. Also a second schema file plus a completeness module is a second place defining what a manifest is, which cuts against the single-schema rule.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Drop the three-tier system, the second schema, the 'Description complete' status and the new-submission hard gate. Build only these, in order: (1) Enforce what the Submit page already promises: submit.md says 'has a license' but catalogue.resolve silently accepts none and details_list prints 'Not stated'. Make a missing license an AppProblem in the submission bot (submit_app.check) and a reported warning in the daily build, not a silent row; keep the 'Not stated' row only for apps already listed. (2) Show absence on the page instead of scoring it: once S2-S4 fields exist, each absent optional fact gets an explicit 'Not stated by the authors' row (Works with, Produces, Limitations, Status) following the License precedent; that is the visible-missing mechanism, with no new badge and no tier. (3) Bot: print non-blocking warning lines (same style as the icon warning) listing the recommended fields an app has not given, from one small tuple in config.py that names schema properties (so it cannot drift from the schema); do not block. (4) Submit page: replace the vague 'full schema lists every field' with a short table Required / Recommended (shown as 'Not stated' when missing) / Optional, and a test that the example YAML in content/submit.md validates against the schema (no such test exists today; verified by grep of tests/). Revisit a hard gate for new apps only after the initialiser form and template check collect the new fields. Maintainer = repo owner is already shown via the GitHub pill; add nothing.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Low if the fields are optional, author-written and shown as 'Not stated by the authors' when absent. Risk: tier-2 'required' wording or a 'Works with' heading could read as a tested guarantee; word it as 'The authors say it works with', and keep it plain text. Capping at 6 x 200 chars is sound; do not add example_data until an author actually has data to point to (YAGNI: 0 of 6 repos expose a dataset link in a manifest).
verdicts.refined_proposal: Add optional `inputs`, `outputs` and `limitations` (array of 1-6 strings, 5-200 chars, same shape as quickstart) to the schema. FIRST update the vendored copies (src-template/.tools/schema/ and LabConstrictor_streamlit/schemas/) and republish the schema, because additionalProperties:false makes any author who adds a field fail their template check and the bot until those copies match; ship in that order. Render 'Works with' and 'Produces' rows plus a 'Limitations' h2 in a new small module (pages_fit.py), each absent field printed as 'Not stated by the authors' (no silent omission). Add the three to cards.search_text. Add a DESIGN.md pattern first. Do NOT add example_data now (leave for when an author asks; the author can already put a link in quickstart or docs_url). Then the maintainers fill the 4 apps' manifests from their own repos (NucleiSky docs/limitations.md, GuessTheCondition README TIFF layout, CellTracksColab README formats table), which is the real fix; do not write those values from the site side.

This is a DESIGN.md Images rule break today (rule: product screenshots have a description in alt) that check_design.py does not catch because it only requires the attribute to exist (check_design.py:162 tests alt is None only); also tighten that check so a figure image in main with empty alt fails. No new field. (2) has_issues: read repo['has_issues'] in catalogue.resolve, store it in the snapshot (bump SNAPSHOT_FORMAT), and in details_list print the 'Report a problem' link only when true, else 'No issue tracker on GitHub'. Zero author input, bug fix for a dead link. verdicts.misleading_risk: High for the existing text: cards.host_badge/host_chip print 'Soon in napari/Fiji/QuPath' for every non-notebook host, which the site invents. GuessTheCondition's own README (line 57) says napari and Fiji already show its tools, yet /apps/guessthecondition/ prints 'Soon in Fiji' and 'Soon in napari'. That is a false statement today. The proposed local-vs-cloud sentence about Google's servers is a site claim about a third party's data handling that nobody here has verified; it could be wrong or go stale. A second status vocabulary beside labconstrictor-project.schema.json (Experimental, Available, Install from GitHub, Deprecated) would show two inconsistent sets on one site.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Split into a bug fix and a small optional field. (1) Immediately remove the invented claim: change the host badge and chip text from 'Soon in X' to a neutral author-claimed wording such as 'Tools for X' / 'Listed for X' (cards.py:63-71 and the DESIGN.md Badges row), with no maturity implied. This needs no schema change and fixes a false statement. Rename the details row 'Status' to 'Verification' so it stops reading as development status. (2) Add one optional field `status` reusing the SAME vocabulary as the project schema (Experimental, Available, Deprecated; do not invent 'stable/in-development/discontinued') and show it as 'Development status: <value>' or 'Not stated by the authors'. (3) Defer `integrations` (per-host status and tested_with) and `requirements.gpu`: add them only when an app author asks, since the bare `hosts` list plus the app's docs is enough for a 6-app catalogue; document in the Submit page that hosts means 'the app's tools are registered for that program'. (4) Drop the site-written 'Colab: files are handled by Google's servers' sentence; if a cloud disclosure is wanted, use a neutral link to Colab's own terms in data/hosts.yaml, not a data-handling claim. Update the vendored schemas first (as in S2) before any author uses `status`.
